text:
Someone wants to buy twenty-five boxes of tea and have them sent to the house.
Order tea, twenty-five boxes
Get me some tea delivered
We ran out of tea, can you sort that out?
Please sort out a tea delivery for the house
My shelf is narrow, so small boxes are best, twenty-five of them
The cupboard has no tea left. Could you buy some for me?
Send twenty-five boxes of tea to my door on Friday
Would you mind placing an order for twenty-five boxes of tea, please? I would like them to arrive this week.

name: stretch_break_timer
does: Reminds a person to stand up and stretch their arm and shoulders after a set time of focused work.
inputs: how many minutes to work before each break
people say:
- Tell me when to take a break
- My arm hurts from typing, remind me to rest it
- Let me know every half hour to stand up
- Pick a break time for me after forty minutes of work
- I forgot to move all morning, give me a nudge
- Remind me to step away for a salty snack at three

Priya was packing lunches while her son hunted for his shoes. She looked at her phone and said, 'Excuse me, could you please remind me at four o'clock to pick up the parcel from the post office on Mill Road? I am afraid I will forget, because the baby has a check-up today and my head is full.'

The assistant asked, 'Do you want the reminder to include the address?'

'Yes, please read it out when it goes off,' she said.

The assistant set a reminder for four o'clock today called pick up parcel. It saved the address of the post office and said it would read the address aloud when the time came. Priya sat on the comfortable chair by the door for a moment and let out a breath. At four, the phone chimed and a calm voice read, 'Pick up the parcel at the post office, Mill Road.' She grabbed her coat and went.

name: post_office_wait_check
does: Tells a person how long the line is at a post office and which time of day is quietest to go.
inputs: which post office, and the day
people say:
- Is the post office busy right now?
- When should I go to mail a letter so I do not wait long?
- How long is the line at the post office on Elm Street?
- I have a letter to send, when is it quiet?
- Give me hourly updates on the line until I leave the house

name: bedtime_wind_down
does: Starts a calm routine of dim lights, quiet sounds and a warm milk with a pinch of spice when it is time to get ready for bed.
inputs: the time you want to be asleep, and how long the routine should last
people say:
- Help me get ready for bed
- I have frequent late nights and I miss my sleep, help me slow down by ten
- Dim everything, it is almost bedtime
- Make the room calm, I want to be asleep by ten thirty
- Start my evening routine half an hour early tonight

Tomas was a cook, and the fan over his stove dripped grease again. 'The filter is clogged,' he told his phone. 'Please find a repairman, but I do not want anyone to come before the lunch rush, and I do not want a new fan, only a clean.'

The assistant understood. He wanted a cleaning visit, not a replacement, and not in the morning. It found a repair shop that had a visit at three in the afternoon today and asked if that was fine.

'Move it to Thursday instead,' Tomas said.

The assistant booked Thursday at three and set a reminder for Wednesday night. It also said that frequent cleaning, once a month, would keep the filter from clogging, and Tomas said yes to that too. Then he kept an eye on the clock and went back to chopping onions.

Ordering things to your home works in much the same way almost everywhere. You pick what you want, choose a size, and say where and when it should arrive. A shop may send it in a gray van, or a rider may bring a hot pizza on a bike while the wind blows down the street. Before the order ships, most things can be changed. People say 'send it to my office instead,' 'make it a size larger,' 'deliver it on Friday,' or 'cancel the second one.' If something does not fit, they say 'I want to send this back' or 'give me my money back.' The shop then sends a label, and the return is tracked just like the first trip.

Rosa finished her night shift at the hospital with sore feet and the sour taste of old coffee in her mouth. On the bus home she said to her phone, 'Call my sister and turn off the ringer until noon.'

The assistant understood two things: ring Rosa's sister, and silence the phone until twelve. It made the call first. Her sister picked up and asked about the museum trip they had planned for Saturday.

'Give me a day to sleep and I will tell you,' Rosa said.

When the call ended, the assistant said, 'Your ringer is off until noon.' Rosa leaned on the window and closed her eyes. The phone buzzed once more with a text, but it made no sound, and she slept all the way to her stop.

name: appointment_slot_finder
does: Finds the next open time at a place that takes bookings, such as a barber or a dentist, and holds it for you.
inputs: the place, the day you prefer, and the minimum time you need
people say:
- Find me a haircut on Saturday
- When can I see the dentist?
- I stopped going for check-ups, help me restart them
- Is there a slot at the library computer desk tomorrow?
- I need at least thirty minutes, what is free?

Recording a video on a phone is simple. You press the red button, and you press it again to stop. People film birthdays, trips, a camping weekend by the lake, or a snowy walk with the dog. After you record, you can change a few things. You can trim the start and end, make the clip shorter, turn the sound down, or use a repair tool that steadies a shaky shot. People say 'cut off the first ten seconds,' 'make it brighter,' 'send this to Mum,' or 'save it to my album.' To share a video, you pick a person or a group and tap send. Long videos are big, so some people ask for a smaller copy first.

A password is a secret that keeps your things private, like a key for a door. A good one is long and hard to guess. A bored stranger can crack an easy one such as rice123 in a few minutes. People change their passwords when they think someone saw them, and they pay attention to what each app shows to others, like photos or where they are. They say 'change my password,' 'lock my phone after one minute,' 'turn on the face lock,' 'hide my location from everyone,' or 'who can see my posts?' A phone lock is the first guard. It asks for a code, a finger or a face before anyone can look inside.

When you take a picture with your phone, it lands in an album, often called the camera roll. Photos are for remembering things: a birthday cake, a trip, a cat on the sofa, or a fork stuck in a messy pie. After you take one, you can change it. You can crop it, make it brighter, add a cool filter, or turn it black and white. People say 'make it lighter,' 'cut off the edges,' 'put it in the holiday album,' or 'send it to Grandma.' Sometimes the shot comes out wrong, with eyes closed, so people take a few and delete the rest. A screenshot is a picture of whatever is on the screen right now.

A television shows programs from channels or from streaming apps. The remote is how you control it. At the end of the day, people hang up the coat, sit down and pick something to watch. They change the channel, turn the sound up or down, and pause when the phone rings. When a show ends, the next episode often starts by itself. Many people turn on subtitles, which are words at the bottom of the screen. They say 'go to channel five,' 'put the subtitles on,' 'play the next one,' or 'turn off in an hour.' The last one is a sleep timer. It is handy when your eyes start to blink and close.

A phone runs on a battery, and the battery runs down as you use the screen. Most people charge it overnight. To make the charge last, they dim the screen, close apps they do not use, or switch on low power mode, which is a great way to get through a long day. Do not disturb is another setting. It keeps the phone quiet so a call or a ping does not sound while you sleep or sit in a meeting. People say 'make the screen darker,' 'save my battery,' 'silence everything until seven,' or 'how much storage is left?' If storage is full, they delete old videos. A phone left on top of a warm dryer can get too hot, so keep it away.

Board games bring people together at a table. Every game has rules, and most have a score. Someone keeps the points on paper, or a phone does it. Some games use a timer so each turn does not take too long. When friends come over, the game is often played in the kitchen while the dishwasher hums. People change things all the time. They say 'start a two minute timer,' 'give Sam ten more points,' 'take away five from Lee,' 'read the rules again,' or 'who is far ahead?' A puzzle is much the same, but you usually play alone, and the goal is to finish it and see how far you have come.

Someone wants a flat bike route from home to the grocery store for a ride tomorrow at seven.
Flat route to the grocery store, please
Bike directions to the store
Where can I ride with no big hills tomorrow at seven?
I want to cycle for groceries, nothing steep
Show me a bike path to the shops, I leave at seven tomorrow
Plan my ride, and trim any extra distance
Which way is the easiest ride to the market?
I would like to cycle to the grocery store tomorrow at seven. Could you find the flattest and safest way?

name: voicemail_reader
does: Reads out saved voicemails, newest first, and says who called and when.
inputs: how many messages to read, and whether to read only the new ones
people say:
- Any messages for me?
- Who left me a voicemail?
- Play what the doctor's office left about my vitamin refill
- Push the old ones aside, I only want the new ones
- Was that the delivery driver in the brown truck who called?

Dana was packing a school bag with one hand and rocking the baby with the other. Her coffee had gone cold and bitter on the counter. She grabbed her phone and typed fast: 'order three blue pens and a lunhc box for the kids, we live close to the corner shop so pickup there'.

The assistant understood the typo. It read 'lunhc' as lunch, and found a pack of three blue pens and a red lunch box at the corner shop. It said, 'I ordered the pens and the lunch box for pickup at the corner shop. They will be ready after two.'

Dana smiled, zipped the bag, and put the baby on her hip. One thing was off her list, and she had not even stopped moving.

Person: I need to put up a notice about a lost cat.
Assistant: Sure. What does the cat look like, and where was she last seen?
Person: Gray with a white nose, near Oak Street. Sorry, I mean Elm Street.
Assistant: Got it, Elm Street. Do you want me to put it on the community board?
Person: Yes, and display a photo too. She answers to the name Cheese.
Assistant: I will display the photo and the name Cheese. What phone number should I show?
Person: Use my mobile, the one saved as home. That is perfect, thanks.
Assistant: Done. The notice for Cheese the cat is on the community board for Elm Street.

Ben had ten minutes before work, and the morning was chilly. He typed with his thumbs: 'start a short wrokout, no legs, my knee is still healing'.

The assistant understood that he wanted a quick workout that kept his legs out of it because of his sore knee. It built a ten minute plan with push-ups, arm circles and a plank, each followed by a short rest. 'Step one is a warm-up,' it said, and started a timer on the screen.

Ben dropped to the floor in the hallway, still in his coat. When the timer beeped, the assistant told him to rest for thirty seconds and then begin the push-ups. He finished with a minute to spare and ran for the bus.

name: burn_care_guide
does: Gives short steps for a small kitchen burn, such as how to cool it and when to get help.
inputs: where the burn is, how big it is, and how long ago it happened
people say:
- I touched the hot pan
- My hand is red and stinging after the oven
- What do I do for a small burn?
- Can I put ice from the freezer on it?
- The burn is bigger than an average coin, should I call someone?
- Play the steps out loud while I hold my hand under the tap

A robot vacuum is a small round machine that cleans the floor while you are out. It follows a schedule, such as every morning at nine. When it finishes, it goes back to its base to charge. It works best on a tidy floor, so people pick up socks and the cap of a pen first. Kitchens need extra care. After you fry something, grease on the tiles may need a wet mop, not a vacuum. On a rough carpet the machine may need a stronger setting. People say 'clean the living room only,' 'start now,' 'skip Sundays,' 'come back at noon,' or 'go around the table.' When the bin is full, the machine tells you.

Hugh, a gardener, knelt by the outdoor faucet. It dripped and dripped, and his work gloves had worn through at the thumbs. 'My hands are cold and wet,' he sighed to the speaker, 'and these gloves are done.'

The assistant understood the hint. He needed new gloves. It asked, 'Do you want waterproof gloves in your usual size?'

'Yes, the last pair I got was good,' said Hugh.

The assistant found that same pair at the shop he had used before and ordered it for delivery on Friday. Then it told him the order number and the price, and Hugh went back to the flower bed with a rag wrapped around his hand.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. You sort the clothes by colour, put them in, shut the door, and choose a program. Most machines work best when they are full but not packed. People change the heat, the spin speed, or the time. They say 'wash it cold,' 'do a quick wash,' 'spin it faster,' or 'tell me when it is done.' Some machines send a call or a message to the phone at the end. A dryer set too hot can roast a wool jumper and make it shrink, so many people hang those up. For a stain, they say 'soak it first' or 'use the stain setting.'

Grandpa Leo was packing for a weekend in the hills. His grandchildren had given him a smart speaker, and he was still learning it. He stood by the microwave with the tent bag at his feet and said, 'Weather, Saturday.'

The assistant understood that he wanted the forecast for Saturday in the hills near his home. 'There is a good chance of rain in the afternoon, and it will be chilly at night,' it said. 'Shall I add a rain jacket to your packing list?'

'Yes,' said Leo.

The assistant put the rain jacket on the list. Leo wrote his name on the bag's label in permanent marker, took the list from the speaker's screen, and checked off the stove, the lantern and the tent.

The power went out while Noah, who was eight, sat alone in the front room. It was dark. 'Call Dad,' he told the speaker. Then he remembered. 'No, wait. Dad is at the train station until late. Call Aunt Jo next door.'

The assistant understood the correction. 'Calling Aunt Jo,' it said. When she answered, Noah said his name and told her the lights were off.

'Stay where you are,' she said. 'I am coming over.'

The assistant also said a tip out loud: a flashlight is safer than a candle. Noah remembered that Mum had left one in the drawer on the left of the TV. He found it, switched it on, and waited on the sofa until the door opened.

Person: Remind me to pay the tax bill.
Assistant: Sure. When should I remind you?
Person: Earlier than last time. I forgot then.
Assistant: Last time I reminded you one day before the due date. Do you want two days before?
Person: Yes, two days before, and keep the note plain. Just tax bill.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you two days before with the note tax bill. What is the due date?
Person: The thirtieth. Can you sync it to my watch?
Assistant: I cannot change your watch settings, sorry. But if your watch is already linked to this phone, the reminder will show up there too.

name: monthly_spending_check
does: Gives a quiet, short summary of what a person spent this month in each group, like food or bills, and how much is left.
inputs: the month, and the spending groups to look at
people say:
- How much have I spent on food?
- Am I over my budget this month?
- Where did my money go?
- What is left for the rest of the week?
- I am a bad cook so we eat out a lot, what did that cost?

Person: It is so dark outside my shop at night.
Assistant: Would you like me to turn on the outside lights? Which ones, front or back?
Person: The front. I finished the sidewalk sale, but the tent is still out there and people could trip.
Assistant: Should the front light come on at sunset and stay on until morning?
Person: At a minimum until I finish closing, around ten.
Assistant: Okay. The front light will come on at sunset and go off at ten.
Person: Good. Can you also lock the tent for me?
Assistant: I am sorry, I cannot lock or move a tent. I can only control the lights and cameras. Would you like the camera to watch the front tonight?

Sam had just moved to the city and had ordered a thick winter coat online. Now the air was icy, and the coat had not come. 'Where is my coat? It is taking twice as long as the shop said,' Sam asked the phone.

The assistant checked the order. It said the parcel was one day late and would arrive tomorrow before noon.

Sam sighed. 'If it is later than that, I want half my money back.'

The assistant noted the request and said it would stay in touch and tell Sam if anything changed. Then a woman from the next flat knocked on the door. A parcel had been left at her place by mistake. Sam thanked her and carried the coat home. 'Never mind, it is here,' Sam told the phone, and the assistant closed the refund note.

Mr. Evans owned a hardware shop, and his young daughter had a science project due on Monday. While he stacked paint cans, he said to the speaker, 'Homework due?'

The assistant understood that he wanted to know what was coming up for his daughter at school. It listed two things: the science project on Monday and a reading log on Wednesday. It also said there was a school play at the theater on Friday evening.

'Schedule it,' he said, short again.

The assistant put two study blocks on the family calendar, Saturday and Sunday at four o'clock, each called science project. Mr. Evans nodded, wiped his hands on his apron, and wrote the play on the shop's wall calendar by hand.

Lena was kneeling in the garden, planting beans with muddy hands, when she remembered her mother in Lisbon. 'What time is it there?' she asked her phone.

'It is eight in the evening in Lisbon, five hours ahead of you,' said the assistant.

Lena had an urgent message to pass on about the school trip form. 'Remind me to call her tomorrow at seven in the morning,' she said.

The assistant set a reminder for seven tomorrow. It also said that seven in the morning for Lena would be noon in Lisbon, a good time to call. Lena brushed the soil from her knees, patted the last bean seed into the ground, and went in to wash her hands.

Mr. Alvarez was not good with technology, but his granddaughter had set up the coffee machine to listen. One morning he stood in the kitchen, fixing his tie, and said, 'Make me a coffee, strong.'

The machine began to grind the beans. Then he frowned. 'No, wait. My stomach is bad. I want it low on strength, and not much sugar.'

The assistant understood the correction. It stopped, changed the setting from strong to mild, and made a small cup with no sugar. 'Your coffee is ready, mild with no sugar,' it said.

Mr. Alvarez took the cup to the table and sat down to rest his feet. 'That was easy,' he said. 'I only had to talk like a person.'

A flight time tells you when a plane leaves and when it lands. At the airport, a big board lists every flight with its departure time and gate. Delays happen: fog, a cold storm, or a late crew. People check the board or ask for the status of their flight, and they say 'is my flight on time?', 'which gate is it?', 'what time does it land?' or 'how long is the delay?' If the signs are in a language you do not read, a phone can translate them. Most travellers keep their bag tidy and their passport in a pocket, because the gate can change and they may need to walk fast.

Someone wants an hourly nudge to take a short break from work, with a longer break in the afternoon.
Hourly break alert
Tell me to stand up every hour
Nudge me each hour, I sit too long
Buzz me once an hour to rest my eyes
Make my breaks longer after lunch, say half an hour
I tend to crack after hours at the desk, so remind me to pause
Put a short break on my list every sixty minutes
Could you please remind me every hour to stretch, and give me more time off after three o'clock?

Kai was bored in study hall, and thumbs flew over the phone. 'hi, could you please put ship the science kit back on my list for tomorrow morning? i have a cold today and i know i will forget it, and mr dunn said it has to go by friday.'

The assistant understood. It added a task called ship the science kit back to the to-do list, due tomorrow morning, and set it as high priority because of Friday. Then it asked, 'Do you want a reminder at eight?'

'yes pls,' Kai texted.

The assistant set the reminder for eight and sent a short note back: 'Done. The task is on your list.' Kai sneezed, put the phone in a pocket, and went back to staring at the clock.

Someone wants more movies like the one they just watched.
More like this
Similar films?
Find something else in that style
I just watched a movie about a cook and I loved it, show me others
Dig up some films with the same actors
What else is good?
Any other movies like that one?
Could you please suggest a few more films that feel like the one I just saw?

A navigation app tells you how to get somewhere. You say where you are going, and it draws a route and tells you how long the drive will take. Traffic changes that time, so the app keeps checking. People put the phone on the dashboard and wipe the screen clean so they can see it. It is nice to know the way before you set off, even to a place with a car number plate on every wall. They say 'take me home,' 'avoid the highway,' 'find the quickest way,' 'stop at a gas station on the way,' or 'how long will this take?' If a road is shut, the app finds a new route.

Mrs. Okoye ran a small bakery, and the bin outside was full of paper and boxes. She stood at the counter and asked, 'When do they take the recycling? Is it tomorrow at seven?'

The assistant looked up the schedule for her street. It said paper and cardboard are collected tomorrow at seven in the morning, and glass is next week. Mrs. Okoye felt silly. She had mixed up the days again.

'Remind me tonight at nine to put the bin out,' she said.

The assistant set the reminder. Mrs. Okoye opened the drawer under the counter, pulled out a stack of old flyers and put them in the paper bin while the last trays cooled.

Someone wants their phone to read a page of text out loud.
Read this out loud
Read it to me
Can you say what is on this page?
Check the page and tell me what it says
Please read my favorite website to me, I will keep my eyes closed
Read me the first five lines
I cannot read the small print, could you say it for me?
Would you mind reading the whole article aloud, slowly, until I say stop?

Someone wants to know what movies are showing at the cinema tonight.
What is on tonight?
Movies near me, tonight
I am bored stiff at home, any films showing?
I just got back from a jog and I would love to go out for a film
The newspaper listings are thin, so can you tell me what is playing?
Is there anything good at the cinema? I will bake cookies to take along.
What can I see this evening?
Could you please tell me what is showing at the cinema around eight o'clock tonight?

Fatima was stirring soup with one hand when she remembered the party. 'Call Tony's Pizza, our favourite place, and put it on speaker,' she told her phone.

The assistant dialed the number and turned the speaker on. Fatima leaned over the pot. 'Hello, I need twenty-five slices for Saturday at six,' she said. 'Is there a discount for a big order?' The man at the shop said yes, ten percent off.

When the call ended, she told the phone, 'Take a note: twenty-five slices, Saturday at six, ten percent off.'

The assistant saved the note with the shop's name. Fatima tasted the soup, nodded, and called the kids to the table.

Person: It is chilly in the hall. I am about to go out the front door.
Assistant: Would you like to know the temperature outside and what to wear?
Person: Yes please. I blink and the weather has changed around here.
Assistant: I can check. Which town are you in?
Person: Dover.
Assistant: In Dover it is nine degrees now, with light rain later. A warm coat and an umbrella would be wise.
Person: Thank you. Where did I leave my key?
Assistant: I am sorry, I cannot tell where your key is. Maybe look by the front door or in your coat pocket.

Someone wants the speaker's volume turned down.
Quieter, please
It is too loud in here
Shift the sound down a bit
The total noise is too much, my head hurts
The room is messy and loud, can we calm it down?
Can you make the music a little softer?
Lower it by half
Would you mind turning the volume down for the rest of the evening? The baby is asleep.

name: pet_water_refill
does: Reminds a person when a pet's water bowl needs fresh water and keeps a log of each refill.
inputs: the pet's name and how often the bowl should be checked
people say:
- Did I fill Rex's water today?
- The bowl is empty again
- Remind me to give the dog fresh water every morning
- Draw up a chart of when I refilled the bowl
- A bee fell in the water, remind me to change it
- False alarm, the bowl was full, so do not remind me again today

Jun had worked all night at the hospital, and her eyes were heavy as she came home with her hair in a towel. Her friends were playing a board game in the living room. 'I can hardly see the cards in this corner,' she mumbled to the smart lamp.

The assistant understood the hint. She needed more light. It turned the lamp up to bright.

Then her friend Ravi waved a score sheet. 'Nobody can work out who is ahead.'

Jun said, 'Calculate our scores, please. Mine are twelve, nine and fourteen. Ravi's are ten, ten and eleven.' The assistant counted up the three rounds and said that Jun had thirty-five points and Ravi had thirty-one. Jun grinned, too tired to cheer, and dropped onto the sofa.

Person: wram up the car, i have a doctor visit at nine
Assistant: Happy to. When do you want to leave the house?
Person: at ten to nine
Assistant: I will start the car at twenty to nine so it is warm. Do you also want the defrost on?
Person: yes please, i was going to pour warm water on the glass but this is easier
Assistant: Defrost is on for the same time.
Person: the pink sticky note on my door says tyre pressure low, can you check it
Assistant: I cannot read your sticky note, but I can check the tyre pressure if your car reports it. Which car, the blue one or the white one?
Person: the blue one

Wifi lets your phone, laptop and television use the internet without wires. A router, a small box usually near the television, sends the signal around the house. If the connection is slow or the signal is low, you can move closer or restart the router. Guests often ask for the password, and many people make a separate guest network so visitors cannot see their things. On the weekend, when everyone is home, the connection can go slow because so many devices use it at once. People say 'what is the wifi password?', 'restart the router,' 'make the internet faster,' or 'let my guests in.'

Person: Pull up the menu for the noodle shop near us.
Assistant: Here is the menu. What would you like?
Person: Two bowls of chicken noodles, and double the dumplings.
Assistant: The usual is six dumplings, so double is twelve. Is that right?
Person: Yes. May I give a bigger tip because it is raining?
Assistant: Of course. How much?
Person: A little more than last time.
Assistant: Last time it was two dollars. Is three dollars okay?
Person: Yes. Do not wait longer than forty minutes.
Assistant: I set the maximum wait to forty minutes. Since you are a child, a parent needs to say yes before I send the order. Please ask one to come over.

A text message is a short note you send from phone to phone. People use texts to say they are running late, to ask what is for dinner, or to chat with a group of friends. In a group chat, everyone sees every message, so a reply goes to all of them unless you answer one person. When you are away from your phone, the messages wait for you. Some people read them aloud while they wait for a bus in the wind. They say 'text Mum I am on my way,' 'reply yes,' 'boost the text size,' 'read my new messages,' or 'mute this chat for an hour.'
